trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Shivamogga, M.C.No. 182 of 2015
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1998 and have been living separately since 2007. The husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking dissolution of marriage, which was dismissed by the trial court. This appeal has been filed against that judgment.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can amicably resolve disputes through mediation.
legal_principles.held: Learned counsels have invited the attention of this Court to the report submitted by Shivamogga Mediation Centre.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can agree to a peaceful separation through mutual consent.
legal_principles.held: That both of us have understood the consequences rising therefrom and have conceded for a peaceful separation by the way of mutual consent for divorce.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can agree to a settlement that includes alimony and other terms.
legal_principles.held: That we both are mature enough to understand its implications and have fully understood the contents, effects, consequences, terms and conditions, and have now appeared before the Mediation Proceedings on our own from will

outcome.final_order: The parties have amicably resolved their dispute and the appeal is allowed.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
